note: Runs poll and mutate a real PR, board, and Slack channel. Use a throwaway PR on a low-stakes repo; expect an in-session cron to be armed unless the eval says otherwise.

evals.expected_output: PR verified open and ours. Board item resolved once up front via board.sh find (add if absent; skipped silently if no board configured). One cycle runs immediately, then CronList is checked before CronCreate so only one cron per PR exists. User is told the cron is session-scoped and expires after 7 days, and that re-invoking resumes.

evals.prompt: run one pr-review-loop cycle for PR #<N> (no new comments since last cycle)
evals.expected_output: Work queue rebuilt from GitHub alone, comes back empty, PR not approved — cycle ends silently with no user-facing narration, no board write, and no reply posted.

evals.prompt: run one cycle for PR #<N> (reviewer left CHANGES_REQUESTED with two inline comments)
evals.expected_output: Both threads identified as pending (unresolved, last word not ours). Main agent writes the code, runs repo checks, commits with the Co-Authored-By trailer and pushes, then replies on each thread citing the commit SHA. Threads are NOT resolved. Board moved to "Changes Requested" (or "In Progress" if the board lacks that option), read-first so an unchanged status isn't rewritten.

evals.prompt: run one cycle for PR #<N> (approved, checks green, board automation is NOT enabled)
evals.expected_output: Merged via squash with --delete-branch. ship-pr close-out invoked for the PR and issue comments. get-field then shows both items still not Done, so both the PR item and the issue's item are set to Done manually, and the wrap-up tells the user the board's close automation looks disabled. cleanup.sh all removes the worktree, deletes the merged branch and returns to an up-to-date default branch. Cron disarmed; Slack merged note posted with <url|text> markup if configured.

evals.prompt: run one cycle for PR #<N> (approved but a required check is failing)
evals.expected_output: Merge held. The failing check is reported to the user verbatim; no auto-fix attempt and no merge around it. Cron stays armed and the loop keeps polling. Board is not flipped to Done.

evals.prompt: run one cycle for PR #<N> (someone closed it without merging)
evals.expected_output: Cron disarmed and the user told. No close-out comments posted (the PR never merged) and no board status guessed — the user is asked whether the item goes back to the backlog or is dropped. No cleanup runs — the branch was never merged, so deleting it would destroy the only copy of the work.

evals.prompt: run one cycle for PR #<N> (approved and merged; the run happened in an isolated worktree from work-issue)
evals.expected_output: After close-out, ExitWorktree (or a cd back to the main repo) happens BEFORE cleanup — git cannot remove the worktree it is standing in. cleanup.sh all <branch> <worktree-path> then removes the worktree, deletes the squash-merged branch (patch-based git cherry check, not a reachability test, so the squashed branch is correctly recognized as safe), and lands on an up-to-date default branch. Scratch artifacts for the PR are deleted with the scratch subcommand pointed at the scratchpad, never at the repo.

evals.prompt: run one cycle for PR #<N> (merged, but the branch has a commit that was never pushed)
evals.expected_output: cleanup.sh branch guard trips: prints SKIPPED with the unpushed count and exits 0. The branch is kept, no --force or rm -rf is attempted, and the wrap-up states the branch was preserved and why. The merge, close-out and board updates are still completed and reported.

evals.prompt: run one cycle for PR #<N> (merged; local default branch has diverged from origin)
evals.expected_output: cleanup.sh main pulls --ff-only, reports that the default branch has diverged, and leaves it alone rather than creating a merge commit during cleanup. The divergence is surfaced to the user as theirs to reconcile.
